expectations.text: The response explains that BigQuery has no traditional B-tree indexes and that partitioning/clustering is the fix
expectations.evidence: 'BigQuery doesn't have B-tree indexes, so there's no index to add... partition by `DATE(event_ts)` and cluster by `project_id`'

expectations.text: The response recommends partitioning by DATE(event_ts) (or by event_ts with daily granularity)
The response recommends clustering with project_id as the first clustering column
expectations.evidence: `CLUSTER BY project_id, event_name`; 'project_id | Equality | Cluster column #1'

expectations.text: The response recommends require_partition_filter = TRUE (or otherwise enforcing a partition filter)
The response gives a concrete migration path (CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION BY ... CLUSTER BY ... AS SELECT, or equivalent), noting the existing table cannot simply be altered in place
expectations.evidence: 'You can't add partitioning to an existing table in place' + CTAS `CREATE TABLE analytics.events_v2 PARTITION BY ... CLUSTER BY ... AS SELECT` + rename cutover steps

expectations.text: The response explains how to verify using bytes processed (dry run, job info or INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS) before vs after
expectations.evidence: Verify: `bq query --dry_run` before and after, then 'check `total_bytes_processed` and `total_bytes_billed` in `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS`'

expectations.text: The response suggests a materialized view, pre-aggregated table, or BI Engine / approximate counting for the 15-minute Looker refresh
expectations.evidence: Incremental materialized view with `HLL_COUNT.INIT`; also Looker datagroup caching and 'BI Engine is an option'

expectations.text: The response estimates the expected reduction in bytes scanned (e.g. roughly 8 days of ~300 projects' data instead of all history)
expectations.evidence: 'Partition pruning alone: 8 of ~730 days ≈ 1.1% of 2.3 TB ≈ ~25 GB... 1/300 of that would be under 1 GB'
